instruction: You are given a heat-conduction template `/home/user/Desktop/heat_base/`. Complete a steady thermal analysis from the command line: 1. Modify and create `/home/user/Desktop/heat/`: - Build a rectangular plate geometry - Set different temperature boundary conditions on two sides, with adiabatic conditions on the others - Configure thermal diffusivity and steady solver parameters 2. Run the solver. 3. Extract the centerline temperature distribution and verify linear-distribution theory. 4. Write a post-processing script to output `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt`: - Temperatures at two specified locations: `temp_a, temp_b` - Format: `temp_a, temp_b` 5. Do not use GUI tools. [Software] OpenFOAM is normally used from a shell after sourcing your installation environment (e.g. its `etc/bashrc`); `foamRun -help` verifies solver binaries are available.
